source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Totowa NYM2 campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity and 200,000 square feet of technical space, and nothing about racks, accelerators, or power density.

The two numbers describe a building, not a workload. Six megawatts spread across 200,000 square feet is 30 watts per square foot, a figure that says how much power the operator will sell, not how densely any given hall is packed. The same 6 MW is roughly 150 racks at 40 kW per rack or about 600 racks at 10 kW, and the published spec does not distinguish between those buildings. For AI specifically, that gap is the whole question: training clusters live or die on power density per rack, and density is exactly what is missing here.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which concerns controls over financial reporting. It says nothing about electrical topology, cooling method, or on-site generation, so the campus's fitness for dense training cannot be judged from what is published. No tenant is named.

New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, of which five publish any capacity figure at all. Those five total 111.3 MW, and this campus contributes 6 MW, about five percent, ranking fourth in the state by published megawatts. That 111.3 MW is a floor on the state's data center load, not a measure of it, because most facilities publish nothing. The data covers one operator's disclosure and a partial state tally. It does not cover actual consumption, grid interconnection, or what is built inside the shell.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
